messages:
jordan: Quick ping — PR #68921 updates the connection allocator and changes eviction ordering. Need runtime + infra + security eyes before merging. Can someone from each team weigh in? @jamie @sam @alyssa :eyes:
erin: Link? small summary? CI green?
jamie: I skimmed the diff — allocator now prefers small-slab reuse which should reduce OOMs during high concurrency. looks fine at a glance but need perf numbers under realistic kv-load. can run a quick local replay.
jordan: diff: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/68921 (config flags and allocator.cc)
deploy-bot: CI passed: unit tests 152/152, integration smoke failed on one flaky test (GRPC intermittent) — retry queued.
sam: important for infra: does this change any sysctl or require new cgroups? also how does it interact with eviction BPF changes we rolled last month?
jordan: no sysctl changes. it does change allocation order and adds a small metadata header. should be transparent to cgroups. jamie, can you confirm behavior with new bpf eviction rules?
jamie: will run a quick canary job against staging with eviction bpf enabled. estimating 30–45m to get meaningful traces.
alyssa: security questions: does allocator introduce new serialization endpoints or change any IPC surface? any added user-supplied config that could be abused?
jordan: no new RPCs, config limited to numeric thresholds (max_small_cache_size). plan is to keep default conservative.
alyssa: ok please add a short note to the PR describing the threat assessment and set config knob gated behind feature-flag + org-admin-only. I'll re-review after that.
mike: I can steward canary if someone else can't. prefer to run canary tomorrow morning in the 09:00–11:00 PT merge window.
nerin: (typo) nina: +1 to mike, I can own rollback if canary goes sideways. please add a simple rollback playbook in the PR description.
jordan: noted — will add threat note and rollback steps. jamie, once you have traces can you paste an excerpt of allocator metrics? something like: free_slab_count, small_reuse_hits, small_reuse_misses.
jamie: sure — will paste results here.
jamie: quick local run results (brief): free_slab_count down ~12%, small_reuse_hits up 38%, p50 latencies unchanged, p95 improved ~6%. attaching raw logs to PR.
sam: that looks promising. infra ask: include a canary plan that specifies target stacks, duration, success criteria (#errors < baseline + 5%, p95 latency not worse than +10%).
jordan: will add canary criteria.
alyssa: once PR updated, I can do a security + config gating sign-off within same day.
mike: scheduling canary for 10:00 PT tomorrow if that works for everyone.
nina: noted, I'll be on standby for rollback and monitoring.
jordan: thanks all. planning to hold merge until: runtime perf + canary metrics in thread, infra canary plan added, security threat note + feature-flag, and CI flakes resolved. aiming for merge after successful canary tomorrow. :thumbsup:
erin: small nit: please include a one-line user-impact note for release notes (e.g., "allocator tweak to reduce OOMs under high concurrent load").
jordan: added. will update PR in ~20m.
jamie: update: staging canary started, I'll post metrics in ~40m.
deply-bot: retry: integration smoke tests passed on rerun.
jordan: typo — deploy-bot fixed. thanks.
jamie: canary metrics (snapshot): small_reuse_hits=138K small_reuse_misses=12K free_slab_count=420 p50=12ms p95=48ms baseline_p95=51ms errors=3 baseline_errors=2
sam: metrics look within canary goals. mike, ready to run production canary?
mike: yes running canary now (10:02 PT). I'll monitor for 30m and report.
nina: monitoring dashboards up, set alert on errors > baseline+3 immediately.
ijordan: (typo) jordan: mike reported canary healthy at +30m. infra and security sign-offs present. proceeding to merge in next slot. thanks everyone!
file_notes: PR coordination thread asking runtime/infra/security for targeted review and canary scheduling; short messages, links, metrics; includes bot CI messages.
